ruling.recommended_action: Issue a Ryde voucher of $8.22 to the rider for the unexempt deviation mileage; retain the metered waiting unit ($0.02) and the 0.66 km corridor residual; no account flag.
ruling.reasoning:
RydeTAXI is metered, so extra kilometres flow straight into the fare and route deviations are refundable in cash terms: the trip charged $39.42 for 27.96 km against a 21.5 km optimal route [F1][F8], and two off-route segments are measured — 22:56–23:04 adding 2.46 km and 23:08–23:14 adding 3.37 km [F3][F4], which is the RD-1 breach RD-2 makes refundable.

No segment is excused. The chat record is empty — no in-app message at all [F9] — so no rider message before either segment agrees to it, and the driver's post-trip statement that "the GPS rerouted me" [F10] is not consent (RD-5 requires a rider message sent before the segment, and a driver's own claim of agreement is not consent) nor a reasonable cause under RD-4. Both advocates stipulate ground consent_after_or_none for F3 and F4, and I so find.

Traffic does not exempt either segment: there is no incident near the route in the trip window [F13], and the only records are band 4 (30–39 km/h) speed bands on East Coast Parkway and Airport Boulevard [F11][F12], which are neither band 1–2 severity nor a standalone exemption under RD-4(b) — RD-4(a) fails as the trace shows.

The refund is the unexempt metres at this trip's own rate: distance fare $39.42 ÷ 27.96 km = $1.4099/km [F8][F5]; 2.46 km + 3.37 km = 5.83 km; 5.83 km × $1.4099/km = $8.2197 → $8.22 [F3][F4][F5][RD-2]. The remaining 0.66 km of billed excess ($9.15 was billed on 6.49 km [F5]) is corridor/map-matching difference RD-2 expressly excludes, and neither party claims it.

The $0.02 waiting line is 0.1 min of metered waiting on a RydeTAXI trip [F6]; under RD-3(c) metered waiting time stays with the driver, so no part of it is refunded. No account flag: the driver's 90-day record shows 0 upheld route disputes [F16], so RD-6's "repeated" precondition is not met and the profile fact is not used to decide the case.

segment_findings.reason: No rider message was sent before the 22:56 segment — the chat record contains no in-app messages at all [F9] — and the driver's post-trip statement [F10] is not rider consent; the segment adds 2.46 km and is unexempted under RD-1/RD-5, so its extra_km are refundable under RD-2.

Same reading for the 23:08–23:14 segment: the empty chat record [F9] shows no rider agreement before it, the driver's statement [F10] cannot supply one, and RD-4 gives no cover because no incident is recorded on the replaced stretch [F13]; the extra 3.37 km is refundable under RD-2.

rejected_claims.reason: The published-line-item point [F8] is accepted as far as FARE-1 goes, but it does not dispose of the case: this is a metered RydeTAXI trip and the distance line $39.42/27.96 km [F8] was inflated by unexempt deviations on the 21.5 km optimal route [F1], which RD-2 reaches.

Accepted only as a cap: 5.83 km of segment-added distance [F3][F4] versus 6.49 km billed excess [F5] leaves 0.66 km corridor difference, which RD-2 excludes; it does not reduce the refund owed on the segments themselves.

The empty chat record [F9] is precisely what defeats the driver: with no rider message before either segment there is no consent under RD-5, so F3 and F4 stand as unexempted deviation segments [F3][F4].

Correct on the merits and binding against the driver's own explanation: no incident on the replaced stretch [F13] and band 4 speed records [F11][F12] cannot exempt a segment under RD-4(a)/(b), so F3 and F4 fall to RD-2 [F3][F4].

RD-6 requires a prior upheld route dispute within 90 days [F16]; the driver's 0 upheld disputes mean the repeated-breach precondition is absent and no flag_account attaches, whatever the merits of this deviation.
